content.title: Where Grammarly attaches to the writing
content.body: Grammarly works where text is already being typed rather than in a separate generation window. This repository records delivery across browser extension, Microsoft Office add-in, and desktop app, so checks run inside the document or email being written. The product's own framing positions it as an enhancement tool for writing that already exists, not a generator that creates a document from a prompt. In practice that means it is installed, then left running: corrections and suggestions surface as the sentence forms.

content.title: What Grammarly checks in a paragraph
content.body: This repository's AI-writing comparison records the check surface as grammar, punctuation, spelling, tone detection, clarity, and engagement, and notes that premium rewrites, fluency rephrases, and a plagiarism check sit behind paid tiers. The checks operate on one paragraph at a time, so the tool improves what is written rather than deciding what to write.
items: Tone detection across sentences and whole drafts
Clarity rewrites that cut wordiness from a paragraph
Engagement suggestions for flat or generic phrasing
Fluency rephrases and plagiarism checking on paid tiers

content.title: Style guides and brand tones for teams
content.body: Grammarly's team layer is the part that matters beyond a single writer. This repository's AI-tools guide records a Grammarly Business tier with shared style guides, custom brand tones, and an admin panel, which means a company's preferred terminology, spelling, and voice are enforced while people write instead of in a late editorial pass. The admin panel gives a central place to manage seats and policy, and the shared guides make the guidance travel with the writer's browser rather than sitting in a document nobody reopens. For organizations where many people produce external text, that is the practical difference between a personal corrector and a governed writing layer.

content.title: What Grammarly will not do
content.body: Grammarly does not draft documents from a prompt; this repository's comparison records it as an enhancement tool, so blank-page generation belongs to the other writing tools on these pages. Quality is strongest in English, which the same file records as Grammarly's best-supported language. It corrects and rephrases inside paragraphs, but it does not assemble a research argument, produce citations, or carry a document outline to completion on its own. Buyers comparing it against generators will find a different job entirely: Grammarly finishes writing, it does not start it.

content.title: Two pricing files that disagree
content.body: This review's own fields record Grammarly as freemium with a band of $12-30/mo. Two files in this repository quote entry pricing differently: one records roughly $12 per month for a paid individual plan, another records a higher per-user band for business plans. Because those entries conflict, treat the band as indicative and confirm current pricing with the vendor before budgeting. No figure beyond the band held on this page comes from anywhere else, and nothing on this page is drawn from a use of the product.

content.title: Deployment and what is not on file
content.body: Grammarly is recorded as a hosted product whose API field is marked available, and delivery runs through the browser extension, Office add-in, and desktop app, so text passes through the vendor's service while being checked. No compliance certification appears anywhere in the material assembled for Grammarly, and no such assertion appears here. For a tool that reads correspondence, drafts, and internal documents, the questions worth pressing with the vendor are about data retention on checked text, whether customer content trains shared models, and how deletion is honored across regions.

content.title: Grammarly against the generators
content.body: Eleven pages of comparisons in this repository pair Grammarly with other products. Its traditional antagonists are the chat assistants and generators — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Jasper, Copy.ai, Writesonic — where the trade is breadth of generation against precision of correction. Pairings with creative tools such as Midjourney, Runway, and Synthesia show up mainly as category contrast: they produce images, video, and avatar scripts, while Grammarly only edits text. For a buyer the distinction is simple — if the problem is finished prose drifting off-tone or off-grammar, Grammarly is the narrower and more appropriate instrument.

content.title: Who should install Grammarly, and who should not
content.body: Grammarly fits individuals and teams whose day is mostly written communication: customer-facing staff drafting replies, marketers polishing channel copy, non-native English writers who want support as they compose. It fits organizations that want shared style guides and brand tones enforced at the keyboard rather than by a late review. It does not fit teams that need content generated from a prompt or researchers who need long-form argument and citation management; this repository files that work under the generators instead. The recorded rating is 4.5 out of 5 from 1,460 reviews.

faqs.question: Is Grammarly a generator or an editor?
faqs.answer: An editor. This repository's AI-writing comparison records Grammarly as an enhancement tool for writing that already exists, correcting grammar, tone, and clarity rather than producing documents from a prompt.

faqs.question: Which languages does Grammarly support best?
faqs.answer: English. This repository records English as Grammarly's best-supported language, with strong quality for grammar, punctuation, spelling, and tone suggestions in that language.

faqs.question: What do I get with Grammarly Business?
faqs.answer: Shared style guides, custom brand tones, and an admin panel are recorded in this repository's AI-tools guide for the Business tier, so company writing rules are enforced while people write.

faqs.question: How much does Grammarly cost?
faqs.answer: This page's recorded band is $12-30/mo. Two repository files disagree on entry pricing — one at about $12 monthly for individuals, another at a higher per-user band for business plans — so confirm current pricing with the vendor.

faqs.question: Can Grammarly work inside Microsoft Word and email?
faqs.answer: Yes. This repository records Grammarly as delivered through a browser extension, a Microsoft Office add-in, and a desktop app, so its checks run inside the document or message being written.
